prediction.overall_explanation:
Reviewed the SigningKeys library functions (saveKeysSigs, removeKeysSigs, loadKeysSigs, getKeyOffset, initKeysSigsBuf) for exploitable issues such as unauthorized storage manipulation, storage slot collisions, out-of-bounds memory access leading to controllable corruption, arithmetic bugs, and reentrancy.

The library performs only storage and memory operations and makes no external calls, so reentrancy is not applicable. Index/count validations in saveKeysSigs/removeKeysSigs prevent obvious under/overflow of indices. Storage addressing uses keccak256 over fixed-size values (bytes32,uint256,uint256), avoiding abi.encodePacked ambiguity. The assembly packing/unpacking of 48-byte pubkeys across two storage slots and 96-byte signatures across three slots is internally consistent.

Potential hazards (e.g., loadKeysSigs writing into caller-provided memory buffers) are internal-only and rely on the calling contract to allocate correct buffer sizes; they do not constitute a standalone, permissionless exploit in this library. No concrete exploit path that does not depend on a buggy/unsafe external caller was identified.
